report.summary: Analyzed chunk 7 of 7 of docrefs.py: verify_fix and verify_fixes functions with docstring claims.

handoff.purpose: Define verify_fix and verify_fixes functions with docstring claims about order and behavior.

symbols.name: verify_fixes
symbols.note: Checks denominator first, then per-target verdicts.

claims.text: ORDER IS THE SAFETY PROPERTY. The denominator is checked FIRST.
claims.why: The docstring claims order but verify_fix calls verify_fix_counts directly; denominator check is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Taking the document out withdraws the claim AND lowers ``resolving`` in one move, so a check that asked 'is the claim gone?' first would call that a success and reward exactly the behaviour the island metric already taught this repo to expect.
claims.why: Behavior depends on external functions and metrics not present.

claims.text: Asking about the denominator first makes the deletion visible no matter what it did to the finding.
claims.why: verify_fix does not check denominator; verify_fixes does, but this claim is on verify_fix.

claims.text: Both honest remedies pass: naming the symbol that exists now (``fixed``) and withdrawing the stale claim (``claim_withdrawn``). Neither lowers the count of references that resolve.
claims.why: verify_fix_counts returns FixVerdict with ok=True for both 'fixed' and 'claim_withdrawn' as seen in earlier code (lines ~700-720).

claims.text: ``claim_withdrawn`` is the verdict for a key found in neither list, and that reading is only sound when the target was taken from ``before.broken``: then absence really does mean the sentence went.
claims.why: The logic of key comparison and context of target origin is not fully present; relies on external caller behavior.

claims.text: A caller that reconstructs a target from somewhere else -- a command line, a serialised and TRUNCATED copy in a queue's evidence -- can produce a key that never matched anything, and will be told the claim was honourably withdrawn.
claims.why: Warning about misuse; not verifiable from this code alone.

claims.text: Such a caller must establish independently that the claim was there to withdraw; :mod:`daedalus.spine.docref_gate` does it by requiring the text to be gone from the document.
claims.why: Reference to external module not present.

claims.text: The denominator is a property of the corpus, not of any one reference, so it is asked once and asked FIRST: if the evidence was destroyed, that is the only verdict returned and no per-reference verdict is manufactured to sit beside it looking reassuring.
claims.why: verify_fixes calls check_denominator first and returns early if destroyed is not None.

claims.text: NO EMPTY GREEN. An empty ``targets`` returns ``False``. Verifying nothing is not the same as verifying something and finding it sound, and a gate that passed on zero targets would turn 'we lost the findings' into a green tick -- which is the exact shape of failure the rest of this harness exists to refuse.
claims.why: Code returns False, (destroyed,) if targets is empty because bool(verdicts) is False.

observations.what: verify_fix docstring claims order safety but function does not check denominator; that is done in verify_fixes.
verify_fixes correctly implements the described behavior: check denominator first, empty targets returns False.
